questions.prompt: A page has a site header, navigation, article, and footer. Which element should wrap its unique primary content?

options.text: A single <main> element.
A <section> element with no heading.
A second <header> element.
A <div role="main"> in addition to a native <main>.

questions.explanation: Use one main landmark for the document's dominant content. Site-wide header, navigation, and footer content normally sit outside it; do not duplicate the main landmark.

questions.prompt: The current page is https://example.test/guides/start.html. What does href="../contact.html" resolve to, absent a <base> element?

options.text: https://example.test/guides/contact.html, because the .. segment is ignored.
https://example.test/contact.html, relative to the current document directory.
https://example.test/guides/../contact.html, without path resolution.
A URL relative to the browser's current working directory.

questions.explanation: A relative reference is resolved against the document base URL, normally the current document URL. The parent-directory segment removes /guides/, yielding /contact.html.

questions.prompt: Which link targets the element whose id is "shipping" in the same document?

options.text: Shipping
Shipping
Shipping
Shipping

questions.explanation: A URL fragment beginning with # identifies a target in the current document. The target element's id must match the fragment.

questions.prompt: A search form should produce a bookmarkable results URL such as /search?q=HTML. Which method best fits?

options.text: POST, because query values belong in the request body.
PUT, because submitting a form always replaces a resource.
GET with each input's name omitted.
GET, with named successful controls encoded in the URL query.

questions.explanation: GET is appropriate for retrieval and submits successful named controls in the URL query, making the result shareable and bookmarkable. Do not use GET for sensitive values; URLs can be recorded in history and logs.

questions.prompt: Which label is programmatically associated with the email input shown?

options.text: <label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" name="email">
<label name="email">Email</label><input id="email">
<label>Email</label><input name="email">
<input id="email"><label for="address">Email</label>

questions.explanation: A label's for value must exactly match the labeled control's id. The name attribute is used in form submission, not to associate a label.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a required email input is accurate?

options.text: required guarantees the address exists and can receive mail.
required prevents an empty value, while type=email applies syntax checks but does not verify a mailbox.
type=email automatically makes the field required.
The browser submits the form even when native constraint validation fails.

questions.explanation: The required constraint rejects an empty value, and type=email checks whether a nonempty value has an email-like syntax. Neither constraint verifies that the address exists; server-side validation remains necessary.

questions.prompt: A button inside a form only reveals optional help and must not submit the form. What should its type be?

options.text: type="reset", because reset buttons do not submit.
type="submit", then cancel submission with CSS.
type="button".
No type, because a button inside a form has no default behavior.

questions.explanation: A button associated with a form defaults to submit behavior when its type is omitted. Explicitly set type="button" for an action that should not submit or reset the form.

questions.prompt: Which controls normally contribute a name/value pair when a form is submitted?

options.text: Every visible control, whether enabled or not.
Only controls with an id attribute.
Every checked and unchecked checkbox, plus all submit buttons.
Successful controls, including eligible enabled controls with a name; unchecked checkboxes are omitted.

questions.explanation: Form submission serializes successful controls, generally requiring an applicable name and enabled state. Unchecked checkboxes are not successful; an id alone does not provide a submitted field name.

questions.prompt: In a data table, which markup best identifies the first column as row headers?

options.text: <th scope="row">Ada</th>
Ada
<th scope="col">Ada</th>
Ada

questions.explanation: A th element marks a table header cell, and scope="row" associates it with cells in that row. Bold styling alone does not communicate a header relationship.

questions.prompt: A decorative divider image adds no information. Which alternative text is appropriate?

options.text: Omit the img element's alt attribute so screen readers infer the image.
Use alt="" so assistive technology can ignore the decorative image.
Use the filename as alt text.
Use alt="decorative image" for every decorative image.

questions.explanation: An empty alt attribute marks an image as decorative and prevents its filename or irrelevant description from being announced. Informative images instead need context-appropriate text alternatives.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of sizes when an img uses width-descriptor candidates such as photo-480.jpg 480w?

options.text: It sets the image's intrinsic pixel dimensions in the file.
It guarantees the browser downloads only the smallest candidate.
It describes the expected rendered slot width at media conditions so the browser can choose a candidate.
It replaces the need for src or srcset.

questions.explanation: With width descriptors, sizes tells the browser the image's expected rendered slot width at specified conditions. The browser combines that information with device pixel ratio and available candidates to choose a resource.

questions.prompt: Which element supplies a caption text track for a video?

options.text: <source kind="captions" src="captions.vtt">
<caption src="captions.vtt">
<figcaption src="captions.vtt">
<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en">

questions.explanation: A track element references a WebVTT text track. kind="captions" identifies captions, and srclang gives the track's language; a source element instead identifies media resources.

questions.prompt: A clickable action saves a draft. Which implementation provides native button semantics and keyboard behavior?

options.text: <button type="button">Save draft</button>
Save draft
Save draft
Save draft

questions.explanation: A native button is focusable and keyboard-operable by default and exposes button semantics. A generic div or span requires additional interaction, focus, and state handling; an anchor represents navigation.

questions.prompt: Which viewport declaration is a common starting point for a responsive page?

options.text: <meta name="viewport" content="width=1024">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<meta charset="viewport">
<meta name="device-width" content="responsive">

questions.explanation: This viewport declaration sets the layout viewport width to the device width and establishes an initial scale of 1. It supports responsive layout; it does not itself make fixed-width content responsive.

questions.prompt: For a classic external script with defer, when does the browser execute it?

options.text: Immediately, blocking HTML parsing until the file downloads.
Only after the window load event, regardless of document parsing.
After parsing completes, while preserving document order among deferred classic scripts.
Before parsing begins, with execution order determined by download completion.

questions.explanation: A deferred classic external script downloads without blocking parsing and runs after parsing completes, before DOMContentLoaded; multiple deferred classic scripts execute in document order.

questions.prompt: Which iframe attribute provides an accessible name describing the embedded content?

options.text: alt="Office location map"
name="Office location map"
aria-describedby="Office location map"
title="Office location map"

questions.explanation: An iframe's title should describe its embedded content and provides an accessible name for the frame. The alt attribute applies to images, not iframes.

questions.prompt: What does form.checkValidity() return?

options.text: A boolean indicating whether the form's associated controls satisfy their constraints.
A promise that resolves after the server validates the form.
The submitted FormData object.
A boolean that is true only after a successful network submission.

questions.explanation: checkValidity() evaluates the form's associated controls against their constraint validation rules and returns a boolean. It performs no network request; invalid controls can dispatch invalid events.

questions.prompt: A form field appears in the UI but is missing from the request. Which first check is most directly relevant?

options.text: Confirm the field has a unique class name.
Inspect whether it has a name, is enabled, and is a successful control for this submission.
Add an aria-label; that makes the value submit.
Replace its id with a name attribute; IDs are forbidden on form controls.

questions.explanation: A form field's submitted key comes from name, and disabled or otherwise unsuccessful controls are omitted. Inspect the actual request payload in developer tools after checking those conditions.

questions.prompt: What is the best reason to use heading elements in a meaningful hierarchy?

options.text: Heading levels are only visual sizes; accessibility APIs ignore them.
Every page must use exactly one h1 and no other h1 is valid HTML.
Headings expose document structure to users and assistive technology; choose ranks based on section hierarchy, not desired font size.
A heading element automatically creates a navigation link to itself.

questions.explanation: Heading elements expose a navigable outline of section topics. Select the level according to the content hierarchy and style appearance separately; multiple h1 elements are allowed by HTML, though a clear page structure is still important.

questions.prompt: A link opens an external site in a new tab. Which markup follows the project's safe external-link pattern?

options.text: Partner
Partner
Partner
Partner

questions.explanation: For an external link opened in a new tab, this pattern combines noopener to prevent access to the opener, noreferrer to suppress referrer information, and nofollow to avoid passing ranking trust.

questions.prompt: How does a browser use source elements inside picture?

options.text: It checks source elements in order and selects a matching supported candidate, falling back to the nested img.
It downloads every source and composites them together.
It uses the final source regardless of media and type attributes.
It treats picture as a replacement for the required img alternative text.

questions.explanation: The browser evaluates picture's source candidates in order, considering media and type where provided, and uses the first suitable source. The nested img supplies the fallback image and its text alternative.

questions.prompt: What does autocomplete="email" communicate on an email form control?

options.text: It validates the address against the user's mailbox provider.
It is an autofill hint describing the expected kind of value.
It makes the field read-only after the first entry.
It sets the field's submitted name to email.

questions.explanation: autocomplete tokens help browsers and assistive technologies identify a field's purpose and may enable autofill. They do not validate mailbox existence and do not replace the name attribute.

questions.prompt: Which element gives a data table a concise title or description associated with the table?

options.text: <summary> placed inside <table>
<legend> placed inside <table>
<caption> as a child of <table>
<figcaption> as a child of <tbody>

questions.explanation: A caption element is the table's caption and helps identify its subject. It belongs as a child of table, typically before the table sections.

questions.prompt: What is a practical effect of rel="preconnect" on a link to a third-party origin?

options.text: It downloads every resource from that origin before parsing.
It makes the origin same-origin for CORS.
It guarantees that the later request cannot be blocked.
It lets the browser initiate connection setup early; use it selectively because connections consume resources.

questions.explanation: preconnect can start DNS, transport, and TLS setup for an important origin before its first resource request. It is a hint, not a guarantee, and unnecessary connections can waste bandwidth and other resources.

questions.prompt: Which choices support a meaningful semantic page structure?

options.text: Use header and footer for the relevant page or section landmarks.
Use main for the document's dominant content, ordinarily only once.
Use nav for a major group of navigation links.
Replace every div with section, even when the group has no thematic heading.

questions.explanation: Semantic elements communicate structural purpose: header/footer mark relevant introductory or concluding content, main identifies dominant content, and nav identifies a navigation section. Section is not a generic replacement for every div and generally represents a thematic grouping.

questions.prompt: Which statements about links and URL references are correct?

options.text: A root-relative path such as /help starts at the origin's root path.
Every relative URL is resolved from the site's origin root, regardless of a base element.
A fragment such as #details can target an element id in the current document.
A URL fragment is always sent to the server as part of the HTTP request path.

questions.explanation: A leading slash references the origin's root path, while a fragment identifies a location within a document. Relative references use the document base URL, which may be affected by a base element; fragments are handled client-side and are not sent in the HTTP request.

questions.prompt: Which practices make a form's controls easier to understand and validate?

options.text: Use placeholder text as the only label because it remains visible after entry.
Give each user-facing control a visible, programmatically associated label.
Use name attributes for values that should be submitted.
Use native constraints such as required or min where they fit, and validate on the server too.

questions.explanation: Associated labels provide a reliable accessible name, name identifies submitted fields, and native constraints improve client-side feedback. Placeholders are not substitutes for persistent labels, and client-side checks must not replace server validation.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe form submission data accurately?

options.text: A disabled form control is normally omitted from the submitted entry list.
A checked checkbox with a name contributes its value; an unchecked checkbox normally does not.
A control's id is used as the submitted key even when it has no name.
A submit button's name/value can be included when that button is the submitter.

questions.explanation: Disabled controls and unchecked checkboxes are generally excluded from form data. Named checked checkboxes submit their values, and the activated submitter's name/value may be included. id supports document identification and label association, not submission keys.

questions.prompt: Which are sound choices for an accessible data table?

options.text: Use table markup for any visual grid, including a page layout.
Use th for header cells and td for ordinary data cells.
Use scope on row or column headers when it clarifies their relationship.
Use caption to identify the table's subject when a caption is useful.

questions.explanation: Header and data cells should use th and td respectively; scope can clarify row or column associations, and caption can name the table. Tables are for tabular data, not general page layout.

questions.prompt: Which image practices are appropriate?

options.text: Omit alt whenever an image is inside a link.
Use the same long alt text for every candidate in a responsive image set, even if the image's meaning changes.
Use alt="" for an image that is purely decorative and adds no information.
Describe an informative image's relevant meaning in its context rather than mechanically copying its filename.

questions.explanation: An empty alternative keeps decorative images out of the accessibility tree, while informative images need concise context-specific alternatives. An image link still needs an accessible name, usually supplied through its image alt text or other link content.

questions.prompt: Which choices improve the accessibility of interactive HTML?

options.text: Prefer native controls because their roles, keyboard behavior, and states are built in.
Use color alone to distinguish required, invalid, or selected states.
Ensure every form field has a programmatically determinable name.
Keep focus visible and provide keyboard access to custom interactions.

questions.explanation: Native controls provide established semantics and interaction behavior. Accessible names, visible keyboard focus, and keyboard operability help users understand and operate controls; state must not be conveyed by color alone.

questions.prompt: Which statements about ARIA and native HTML semantics are correct?

options.text: Adding role="button" to a div automatically makes it focusable and keyboard-operable.
Native HTML semantics should generally be preferred when an element already expresses the needed role.
ARIA labels always override visible text in every accessibility naming situation.
ARIA can add semantics or state, but it does not automatically implement keyboard interaction.

questions.explanation: Native elements are usually the most robust way to provide semantics and expected behavior. ARIA can expose role, name, or state, but authors remain responsible for focus and interaction; naming precedence depends on the accessible-name rules and element.

questions.prompt: Which resource-loading statements are accurate?

options.text: defer on an external classic script avoids blocking parsing while the file downloads.
async guarantees execution order matching the document order of scripts.
Preload should be reserved for resources needed soon, with the correct as value and compatible resource selection.
A preload guarantees that a resource will be used and improves performance in every case.

questions.explanation: Deferred classic scripts download without blocking parsing and execute after parsing in document order. Preload can prioritize a resource expected soon, but incorrect or unused preloads can waste bandwidth; async scripts execute as they become ready and do not preserve order.

questions.prompt: Which practices are appropriate for embedded content?

options.text: Assume sandbox="allow-scripts" also grants same-origin access.
Give an iframe a concise title describing the embedded page or tool.
Use the iframe title as a substitute for checking whether the embedded content itself is accessible.
Use iframe sandbox restrictions deliberately and grant only needed capabilities.

questions.explanation: A useful title helps identify the frame, while sandbox can restrict embedded capabilities and should be configured to the actual need. allow-scripts alone does not grant same-origin access, and a title does not make the framed page accessible.

questions.prompt: Which browser API practices can help implement and test form behavior?

options.text: Use form.submit() when native constraint validation and submit events must run.
Use new FormData(form) to inspect eligible named form entries.
Use control.validity or checkValidity() to inspect constraint-validation state.
Use form.requestSubmit() when code should request normal submitter behavior and validation.

questions.explanation: FormData collects successful named entries, validity exposes constraint state, and requestSubmit() follows the normal submission path including validation and submit events. The legacy submit() method bypasses constraint validation and does not dispatch a submit event.

questions.prompt: When debugging a form that behaves differently from expectations, which checks are useful?

options.text: Inspect the rendered DOM and the actual network request's method, URL, and payload.
Assume a successful client-side validity check proves the server accepted the data.
Assume the source file alone always shows the final DOM after scripts and parsing.
Check the browser's reported validity state and whether a control is disabled or lacks a name.

questions.explanation: The live DOM and network panel reveal what the browser actually rendered and sent; validity, disabled state, and name explain common submission differences. Client-side checks cannot prove server acceptance, and the source view may differ from the live DOM.

questions.prompt: Match each semantic element to its primary purpose.

columns.label: Dominant content of the document
Major group of navigation links
Content tangentially related to surrounding content
Generic container with no implied semantics

questions.explanation: main identifies dominant document content, nav identifies a section of navigation links, and aside represents content tangentially related to its surrounding content. A generic container is typically a div.

questions.prompt: Match each form feature to the behavior it provides.

rows.label: label with for matching a control id

columns.label: Associates a label with the control
Supplies the field's submitted key
Adds a nonempty-value constraint
Requests normal submission behavior, including validation

questions.explanation: A matching for/id pair provides label association; name identifies submitted data; required adds a constraint against empty values; requestSubmit() invokes the normal submission path, including applicable validation.

questions.prompt: Match each table element or attribute to its typical role.

columns.label: Names or describes the table
Identifies a header for a column
Identifies a header for a row
Marks an ordinary data cell

questions.explanation: A caption supplies a table caption, while th cells with scope="col" or scope="row" declare column or row headers. Ordinary data cells use td.

questions.prompt: Match each resource-loading feature to its described behavior.

rows.label: defer on a classic external script

columns.label: Executes after parsing, preserving order among deferred classic scripts
Executes when ready; ordering relative to other async scripts is not guaranteed
Hints that connection setup to an origin may begin early
Always blocks HTML parsing until window load

questions.explanation: Deferred classic scripts wait until parsing completes and preserve their relative document order; async scripts run when ready without preserving order; preconnect is a connection-setup hint.

questions.prompt: Match each embedded-content feature to its purpose or limitation.

columns.label: Provides a descriptive accessible name for the frame
Restricts capabilities unless permissions are granted
References a text track of captions
Automatically writes a transcript for the video

questions.explanation: An iframe title identifies the frame to users of assistive technology; sandbox restricts embedded capabilities subject to explicitly granted tokens; a captions track points to caption text rather than generating it.

questions.prompt: Match each validation or debugging tool to what it can establish.

columns.label: Whether associated controls satisfy client-side constraints
The form's successful named entries at construction time
The request actually sent, including method and payload
Whether the server accepted and persisted the data

questions.explanation: checkValidity() reports client-side constraint validity, FormData exposes successful named entries, and the network panel shows the actual request. None of these alone proves that the server accepted or persisted the data.
